message.content:
Address the review of open PR #519 in the caliper repo (branch `perf/readonly-from-flags`, head e92b79c3), at the class level. In your worktree: `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c fix-519c origin/perf/readonly-from-flags`; push with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/perf/readonly-from-flags` (normal push, fast-forward, no force). You OWN crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs response side (`SymbolWire`, `SymbolInfo`, `settled_readonly`, `NO_ASSIGNMENT_DECLARATION`, their tests) and crates/semantic/src/convert.rs (`State::readonly`, `Converter::readonly`); do NOT touch the request side of rpc.rs (open PR #521 types the requests: `Ask`, `Request`, its tests) or other files. Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, diagnose-after-three-findings.md and perf-priority-wall-then-memory.md (same dir), AGENTS.md ('Assert content, not presence', non-negotiables 1 and 6), CONTRIBUTING.md (pre-push bar incl. 'Absence is not evidence' and 'Work ahead of a guard'), `gh pr view 519`. Rules: signed commit with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; machine shared (check `uptime`; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/); do not open/edit the PR or poll CI; update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-readonly.md in place (add a 'Review round 3' heading; keep what is true) and I publish it. Final message max 150 words: head SHA, what each item became, blockers. Cap 100 tool calls; never ask questions.

REVIEW ITEMS (read-only code review of e92b79c3; verify each against the code, do not take them on trust): (1) the doc comment on `State::readonly` (convert.rs ~839) says flags are 'kept only for a list with a property its answer does not settle', but `Converter::readonly` memoises every list incl. fully settled ones: make the comment true (or change the code if you judge skipping the memo for a fully settled list is better for memory: measure the Arc<[bool]> cost on Chakra and say). (2) `NO_ASSIGNMENT_DECLARATION` hard-codes tsrs 0.24 syntax-kind numbers; the comment claims the list 'only ever errs toward the checker', which is false for a kind NUMBER reused by another kind after a renumbering (a CallExpression/BinaryExpression number in the list would settle false for a defineProperty/assignment declaration). Make the guard sturdier than 'rerun a test by hand': e.g. a test that runs in every `cargo nextest` (confirm that it does, so CI covers every tsrs bump) and asserts, from the real checker, the kind number of each listed kind AND that the kinds that make a declaration an assignment/defineProperty (CallExpression, BinaryExpression, PropertyAccessExpression, ElementAccessExpression, JSDoc forms as the Go `getAssignmentDeclarationKind` uses) are NOT in the list; also check whether a version-derived guard is feasible (e.g. a const asserting the pinned `tsrs_api` version string equals the one the numbers were taken from, failing the build/test on a bump with a message saying to re-verify): choose the smallest that makes a renumbering fail loudly, and correct the comment's claim. (3) the real-checker agreement test pins `settled(true) >= 20 && settled(false) >= 100`: loose bounds that break 'assert content': replace with the EXACT partition per named property (each `Export.property` -> Settled(true) / Settled(false) / Asked), so a regression that returns None more often, or settles wrongly, fails by name. (4) `transient_unproven` / `modifiers_unread` rely on `check_flags == 0` and presence of `valueDeclaration`; a property with nonzero check flags (e.g. Instantiated alone) and no `valueDeclaration` in the answer would settle false. Settling false for a Property with no value declaration needs POSITIVE evidence it is checker-made WITHOUT a declaration: require a check flag from the set that implies it (Mapped, ReverseMapped, Synthetic property/method, per TypeScript's CheckFlags as tsrs numbers them: read tsrs_checker's `CheckFlags` bitflags in ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/ and the Go `getDeclarationModifierFlagsFromSymbol`) and NOT merely 'any nonzero'; add unit cases (Instantiated alone with no valueDeclaration -> asked) and check on all corpora that the settled share barely changes: Chakra `isReadonlySymbol` count stays about 1,543 (`-vv`, `--collapse-inherited-props none` too) and a temporary check-everything mode (as before, removed before commit) shows 0 disagreements. (5) `Converter::readonly` rejects a short AND a long `isReadonlySymbol` batch as `CallError::Rejected`; the review says `readonly_symbols` already validates the count in `batch`, so the checks cannot fire without a bug, and a Rejected would fail a whole component for a cosmetic flag instead of degrading with a Diagnostic (AGENTS non-negotiable 6). (An earlier review asked for the long-batch check; do what is right: verify whether `batch` validates the count; if it does, replace the two checks with `debug_assert_eq!` on the lengths and a fallback that asks nothing more; if it does not, validate in `readonly_symbols`.) Mutation-prove each new or changed guard. Re-verify: output byte-identical (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) vs a build of origin/main on /Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src,chakra-ui/packages/react/src,shadcn-ui/apps/v4,ant-design/components,react-spectrum/packages}, default and Chakra with `--collapse-inherited-props none`; drop runs whose diagnostics hold a SEMANTIC_BACKEND entry with severity other than info (check code and severity, never message text). Gates by exit code: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (pty/watch tests need the sandbox off), `just test-checker-lane` (outside the sandbox, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR).

description: "Rules every caliper worker follows (scope, branch/push, targeted checks, call cap, PR body, pre-push gate). Copied from the deleted caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md on 2026-11-17; paths to fixtures no longer exist"
metadata:

  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-18T01:13:52.369Z
---

Restored from my reading of `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md` (deleted by the user 2026-11-17; see [[fixtures-is-not-scratch]]). Changes made while restoring: no build output or scratch in `caliper-fixtures`; PR bodies go in `$TMPDIR` or the worktree, not there.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

**Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Plain `rustc` is 1.99.1 here; the old note about the mise shim forcing 1.98.1 did not reproduce on 2026-11-17. Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: <session url>`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, fully qualified when pushing a bare SHA), never `--no-verify`, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Workers do not open or edit the PR and do not poll CI.

**Checks, targeted (CI runs the rest)**: always before push `just lint doc-check machete typos`. Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless that area changed. Tests must fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one. No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, prefer allocation or instruction counts.

**Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

name: diagnose-after-three-findings
description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

name: perf-priority-wall-then-memory
description: "Perf priority order: wall time most, memory also important, CPU only a tie-breaker; judge by addon first-answer and per-story latency as well as whole-project extract"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-23T17:25:30.135Z
---

Wall time matters most to the user; memory (peak RSS) is also important; CPU seconds are a tie-breaker, not a goal. Stated 2026-11-23 while deciding whether rayon threads should be capped or dynamic.

**Why:** the user feels wall time, and Storybook runs beside Vite, the IDE and the TypeScript server, so memory and wasted CPU matter on their machine and on few-core CI runners. A change that lowers CPU but raises wall time is a loss (a fixed rayon cap of 4 cut CPU 17-36% on four corpora but doubled Chakra's wall time).

**How to apply:** accept no wall regression on any corpus; then take the lower peak RSS; then lower CPU. Judge by the addon's first-answer latency (150 ms budget) and per-story median (`gate_harness first-answer`), not only the whole-project `extract` wall time the weekly records. Measure on a quiet machine (load under ~10, swap not full) or compare CPU and counts; see [[measure-memory-and-time]] and [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].
